subject: Dynamic uptime benchmark + pass-through monthly credits for QuantumPay
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@quantumpay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quantumpay.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA baseline and monthly remedy structure

Vivek —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to send our baseline ask so your legal team has something to react to. High level: QuantumPay needs a 99.95% monthly uptime guarantee for our production payments pipeline (multi-region), with a defined monthly service credit schedule tied to measured availability and a clear carveout for scheduled maintenance. We're particularly sensitive to long tail latency spikes for batched reconciliation jobs (p95/p99).

Attached: QuantumPay_SLO_request.pdf (high-level requirements).

Can Redwood provide an annotated SLA template that shows:
- The uptime measurement method (per-region & blended)
- Monthly credit tiers and max cap
- Maintenance windows and notification SLAs
- Any pass-through / third-party credit handling (we prefer pass-through to cover downstream fees)

Appreciate a draft by end of next week. If there are constraints on pass-through credits for marketplace/provider charges, highlight them.

Best,
Sophie Lang
Director, Platform Ops | QuantumPay
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@quantumpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and monthly remedy structure

Sophie —

Thanks, this is helpful. We're attaching a targeted draft (redwood_sla_proposal_v2.pdf) that tries to reconcile your 99.95% target with our standard operational model. Key notes up front:

- Measurement: uptime is calculated as blended availability across your provisioned regions using our standard health checks (per-tenant routing & request sampling). We include a clarified window for measuring reconcilers (batch jobs) so long-tail p99 latency is captured in a latency SLO section versus raw availability.

- Dynamic benchmark: instead of a flat cap we propose a small dynamic uplift band (+/− 0.02%) for months with measured capacity bursts (we flag these and provide a monthly capacity report). That limits surprise credit exposure while still targeting 99.95% as the anchor.

- Monthly credits & pass-through: we can offer pass-through credits for third-party infra charges but need to cap the pass-through to avoid double recovery (we propose a 50% pass-through rate with a monthly cap equal to the remedy band). If you prefer full pass-through we need a rev-share or increased baseline to offset risk.

- Maintenance: 1x scheduled maintenance window per region per month (2 hours, 72-hour notice) by default; emergency maintenance is excluded but requires post-facto report and root cause analysis.

I've included an internal capacity report stub (capacity_report_Q3.xlsx) for how we project reconciliation windows will behave under your projected peak. Ben and Laura are looped for pricing/legal nuance.

If that framing looks ok I can ask Legal to generate a redline-by-section. Happy to run a quick call Thurs 8/27 to walk through.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_proposal_v2.pdf, capacity_report_Q3.xlsx
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@quantumpay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quantumpay.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and monthly remedy structure

Vivek —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from procurement and infra:

1) Dynamic uplift band: procurement is uncomfortable with a variable anchor; can you make the uplift explicit in the SLA and include an example month with calculations? We'll need a deterministic formula to lock into the contract.

2) Pass-through: our preference is full pass-through of third-party charges tied directly to service impact (we operate a tight budget). You mentioned 50% cap — can you share the rationale? Are you able to provide an indemnity or escrow for third-party fees?

3) Latency SLO: adding a p99 capture is good. Can you propose a p95/p99 ladder with explicit credit triggers (e.g., p99 > X ms for > Y% of requests => credit tier)?

procurement has asked me to loop them in on any material change: procurement@quantumpay.com.

If it's helpful, we can do a follow-up call next week; otherwise please send a section-level redline.

Sophie
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@quantumpay.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and monthly remedy structure

Sophie / team —

Wrt pass-through and the uplift band: some background to make the options concrete.

- Why 50% pass-through?: In practice, third-party infra or marketplace credits can themselves be limited (API provider agreements, marketplace T&Cs). A 50% pass-through gives you a meaningful recovery while keeping us from bearing open-ended third-party indemnity risk.

- Alternative structures we can offer (pick one):
  * Full pass-through up to a monthly monetary cap (we would negotiate the cap; example: $50k/mo max)
  * Full pass-through if QuantumPay takes a 6-month term extension or executes a committed-capacity reservation (reduces our variance exposure)
  * 50% pass-through with a rolling 3-month reconciliation (we absorb the first instance each quarter, you get pass-through thereafter)

- Uplift band formula (example): Effective Monthly Uptime Anchor = TargetUptime − max(0, ObservedBurstImpactPct * 0.0001). We can convert that to a worked example in the doc for the most recent capacity report month.

- Latency ladder idea (proposal):
  * p95 > 350ms for > 5% of sampled requests => Tier 1 credit (0.5% of monthly invoice)
  * p99 > 1200ms for > 1% of sampled requests => Tier 2 credit (1.5% of monthly invoice)
  * p99 > 2000ms for > 3% => Tier 3 credit (3% of monthly invoice)

If any of those options is acceptable we'll add the exact numbers into the redline and highlight the places where legal requires reciprocity (term, committed capacity). Laura — can you prepare a short redline with the three structures so Sophie/procurement can pick?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@quantumpay.com>, procurement@quantumpay.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and monthly remedy structure

Sophie / procurement team —

Appreciate the clear asks. Next steps:

1) Laura will circulate a redline with three pass-through options and a worked example of the dynamic uplift formula by EOD Wed (9/1). That will include the p95/p99 ladder Ben sketched.

2) If you select the full pass-through with a cap, we will include an optional committed-capacity credit that reduces the cap by 25% in exchange for a 12-month minimum term. Example numbers will be in the redline.

3) I'll set a 30-minute sync on Thurs 9/2 to walk the procurement team through the math — propose 10:00 AM PT; if that's not OK suggest alternatives.

If procurement agrees preliminarily to any of the three structures, Legal can start clean-sheet redlines; otherwise we'll iterate.

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
